parsed.summary: Both theorems formalize the variable-leaf parts of Theorems 1.2 and 1.3. If a division-free formula over ℂ, with leaves being variables x_ij or complex constants and gates +, −, ×, evaluates to per_n, then it has at least n^4/(128 log2 n) variable leaves (n ≥ 32). If a valid formula with ÷ gates evaluates in ℂ(x_ij) to per_n, then it has at least n^4/(192 log2 n) variable leaves, but only for n > 32. The most important caveat is that the rational-formula theorem drops the paper's case n = 32. A lesser caveat is that the gate-count bounds G(Φ) are not formalized.

glossary.plain: Binary expression tree with leaves x_i or constants c ∈ R and internal gates +, −, ×.
Polynomial in R[x_i] computed by the formula.
Number of variable-labelled leaves, with repetitions counted separately; constants count 0.
Formula tree that additionally allows ÷ gates.
Value of the formula in the rational function field Frac(ℂ[x_ij]).
glossary.note: Division by 0 would give the junk value 0, but Valid excludes it.

glossary.plain: Every ÷ gate, recursively, has a denominator subformula whose value is nonzero in the field.

lean_claims.plain: For n ≥ 32 and any division-free formula f over ℂ with eval f = per_n: n^4/(128·log2 n) ≤ L_var(f).
For n > 32 and any valid rational formula f over ℂ whose value in ℂ(x_ij) equals per_n: n^4/(192·log2 n) ≤ L_var(f).

paper_claims.plain: If n ≥ 32 and a division-free formula Φ computes per_n, then L_var(Φ) ≥ n^4/(128 log2 n) and G(Φ) ≥ n^4/(256 log2 n). The same bounds hold for total leaves and vertices.
If n ≥ 32 and a valid formula Φ with division computes per_n, then L_var(Φ) ≥ n^4/(192 log2 n) and G(Φ) ≥ n^4/(384 log2 n).

coverage.why: The L_var bound matches exactly; the G(Φ) bound is omitted.
Requires n > 32 instead of n ≥ 32, and the G(Φ) bound is omitted.
The circuit bound is not a target.

flags.explanation: The hypothesis is 32 < n, but the paper states n ≥ 32, so the case n = 32 is not covered.
flags.probe_idea: Restate the theorem with (hn : 32 ≤ n) and check whether the proof still goes through.

flags.explanation: The gate-count bounds G(Φ) ≥ n^4/(256 log2 n) and n^4/(384 log2 n) are not formalized. These do not follow trivially from L_var, because many leaves can be constants.
flags.probe_idea: Define a gates function on Formula and state the bound n^4/(256·logb 2 n) ≤ gates f.

Division happens in a field, and the Valid hypothesis requires every denominator to be nonzero.
